what.text: Pumpkin seed oil comes from the seeds of Cucurbita pepo. The authors of the main hair trial note it has been shown to block 5α-reductase and to have antiandrogen effects in rats.

what.text: There is little research on pumpkin seed oil for hair loss: one small trial in men.

research.text: One randomized, placebo-controlled trial in 76 men (2014) and one comparison with minoxidil in 60 women (2021) have been published. The 2014 trial tested a capsule product and was funded by its supplier.

research.title: Pumpkin seed oil capsules in men (Cho et al.)

facts.v: 76 men with mild to moderate androgenetic alopecia; 12 dropped out
400 mg of pumpkin seed oil a day, as a branded capsule product, or placebo
blinded photo assessment, self-assessment, hair thickness and hair count

research.found: Mean hair count rose by 40% on pumpkin seed oil vs 10% on placebo. Self-rated improvement and satisfaction were higher. Adverse effects did not differ. The capsules, the randomization codes and a grant came from the product's supplier. DHT and PSA were not measured. A published comment noted that results for the front of the scalp were not reported.

research.title: Pumpkin seed oil vs minoxidil foam in women (Ibrahim et al.)

facts.v: 60 women with female pattern hair loss (30 per group)
pumpkin seed oil or minoxidil 5% foam

research.found: Both groups had less variation in hair-shaft thickness and fewer vellus hairs after treatment. Regrowing hairs increased in the pumpkin seed oil group.

src.label: Ibrahim et al., J Cosmet Dermatol

research.text: In male mice given testosterone to block hair growth, 10% pumpkin seed oil on the skin for 3 weeks raised hair growth scores and the share of follicles in the growth phase. A 2022 mouse study tested it both on the skin and by mouth. These are animal results only.

us.text: Pumpkin seed oil is not an FDA-approved drug for hair loss or any other use. It can be sold as a dietary supplement. FDA does not have the authority to approve dietary supplements before they are marketed. As of November 1, 2026.

side.text: There is little safety data on pumpkin seed oil for hair loss. The trials reported no difference in side effects from placebo. FDA does not review supplements before they are sold.

items.text: adverse effects did not differ between pumpkin seed oil and placebo over 24 weeks. A questionnaire on erections (IIEF-5) showed no difference between groups.

unconfirmed: The full ingredient list of the branded capsule used in the 2014 trial was not given in the paper's methods, so whether it contained only pumpkin seed oil was not confirmed.
The 2022 mouse study was read only in part (abstract start); its findings are not reported here.
Pumpkin seed oil's status in Canada, the UK and Australia was not checked against a regulator record.
surprises: The single trial behind pumpkin seed oil for male hair loss was 76 men for 24 weeks, funded by the capsule supplier, which also held the randomization codes.
